name: LogRocket
description: LogRocket is a digital experience analytics platform for session replay, issue investigation, product analytics, and frontend monitoring.
agentUseSummary: Connect one exact LogRocket project with a customer-owned project API key, then let agents query only the provider's read-only find_issues MCP tool under approval. Relay excludes sessions, replay watching, metrics, Galileo, account discovery, writes, exports, and raw MCP access.

credentialRequirements.name: LOGROCKET_API_KEY
credentialRequirements.label: LogRocket project API key
credentialRequirements.helpText: Create a dedicated project-scoped API key in LogRocket Settings > API Keys and store it only through Relay's encrypted connection flow.

credentialRequirements.name: LOGROCKET_ORGANIZATION_ID
credentialRequirements.label: LogRocket organization ID
credentialRequirements.helpText: Enter the organization component from the exact project App ID.

credentialRequirements.name: LOGROCKET_PROJECT_ID
credentialRequirements.label: LogRocket project ID
credentialRequirements.helpText: Enter the project component from the exact project App ID.

capabilities.label: Find project issues
capabilities.description: Query one exact project's issue summaries through LogRocket's issues-only MCP toolset.

approvalRequired.label: Find project issues
approvalRequired.description: Call only the dynamically described find_issues tool against one exact project-scoped LogRocket issues endpoint.

blocked.label: Access session recordings
blocked.description: Session discovery, replay watching, user/account targeting, console logs, network bodies, DOM content, and session URLs are blocked.

blocked.label: Use metrics or Galileo
blocked.description: Metrics, natural-language Galileo queries, generated investigations, funnels, heatmaps, dashboards, and arbitrary analytics are blocked.

blocked.label: Access broader LogRocket account data
blocked.description: Organization/project discovery, other projects, users, roles, settings, API keys, audit data, exports, integrations, and administration are blocked.

blocked.label: Use raw or broad MCP access
blocked.description: Raw tool names, tool discovery, unrestricted toolsets, custom MCP origins, pagination, polling, retries, batches, and provider-response pass-through are blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Safe
approvalProfiles.description: The one project-scoped issue query requires approval; session replay, metrics, Galileo, discovery, administration, exports, and raw MCP remain blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Dangerously skip permissions
approvalProfiles.description: The one project-scoped issue query runs without Relay per-action approval; exact project binding, issues-only toolset, dynamic schema check, encrypted key, output bounds, audits, and no-write behavior remain enforced.

providerSetup.blocker: A customer administrator must select one project, create a dedicated project-scoped LogRocket API key, and supply the exact organization/project App ID components. No account, key creation, credential capture, live MCP session, or provider acceptance is available in this worker task.
providerSetup.nextAction: An authorized LogRocket administrator creates a dedicated API key for one project in Settings > API Keys and stores it with the exact project App ID through Relay's encrypted flow. They then separately verify issues-only tool discovery, one approved query, rate limits, key regeneration/revocation, disconnect, and post-disconnect denial.

evidence.supports: LogRocket documents its hosted MCP endpoint, organization/project path scoping, toolset filtering, the exact find_issues tool, OAuth and Bearer API-key authentication, and project-scoped API keys. Relay fixes the URL to one exact project with toolsets=issues and exposes no other remote tool.

LogRocket states that REST API access requires a customer-regenerable access key and describes encryption, request authorization, payload restrictions, rate limiting, logging, SSO, and two-factor support.

LogRocket documents that session recording can contain DOM interaction, network request/response data, performance data, console logs, and application state. Relay therefore blocks session discovery and watching instead of exposing the broad sessions MCP toolset.
